gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a replacement stylus costs per hour of play. Using Audio-Technica's 300-hour replacement rule, the genuine Sony 9-301-000-82 stylus at its $65.95 retail price comes to about $0.22 an hour, or about $0.16 per 45-minute LP. LP Gear's $29.95 replacement comes to about $0.10 an hour. The same figure for the AT-LP70XBT's AT-VMN95C stylus could not be worked out from a page I opened.
standout_why: Turntableverse (rank 1/2, read 2026-11-10) gives prices ($299 AT-LP70XBT, $349.99 Sony PS-LX3BT) and codecs, and names the AT-VMN95C. It gives no stylus life, no replacement-stylus price and no cost per hour. I could not compare against What Hi-Fi? (cited) or Louder (cited) because WebFetch got only each page's title. Vinylpickup failed on an SSL error. So the finding is new against the one rival I could read. But it covers only the Sony side, and the 300-hour figure comes from Audio-Technica, not Sony, so it cannot yet rank the candidates.
decides: It does not decide the pick yet. If the AT-VMN95C costs about $30 in the US, the AT-LP70XBT would cost about half as much per hour as the Sony PS-LX3BT with a genuine Sony stylus ($0.10 vs $0.22). That would support ChatGPT's choice of the AT-LP70XBT. But I opened no page that gives that ~$30 price, and Sony states no stylus life on any page I opened.

findings.label: Official stylus life by tip type
findings.value: Conical/bonded 300–500 h; elliptical 300 h; microlinear 1,000 h; Shibata/special line 800 h
findings.source_title: Audio-Technica AT-VMx manual: Replacing the stylus
findings.note: These are for the AT-VMN10xCB/70xSP (300–500 h), 20xEB/30xEN (300 h), 40xML/45xML (1,000 h) and 50xSH/60xSL (800 h). They are not the VM95 styli the AT-LP70XBT takes. They suggest that a microlinear upgrade lasts about 3× longer, which is the AT-LP70XBT's upgrade path, but they are not a spec for that turntable.
